evidence_quotes.quote: This triggered a dispute over the control of the water sources, which confronted Government institutions and the Atenas and Tacares communities. This article focuses both in the dispute itself and in Government-led attempts to find a negotiated solution to the conflict.

Para esto se caracterizan los actores presentes en las distintas negociaciones entre las partes, las estrategias empleadas en cada caso, y finalmente, la pertinencia o no de este tipo de respuestas institucionales para el procesamiento de demandas políticas ante un conflicto por el uso y gestión de un recurso natural de vital importancia: el agua.

Para los vecinos de Tacares, la causa del conflicto era la implementación de un proyecto con las características de una política pública top-down pues la formulación y el inicio de su ejecución fue a través de una imposición institucional;

Para esto se emplea un diseño de investigación cualitativo a través de entrevistas semiestructuradas a actores de la comunidad de Tacares y a actores institucionales; asimismo se realiza una revisión bibliográfica de actas institucionales y de publicaciones en medios de comunicación locales y nacionales.

Finalmente, tras examinar el conflicto y las negociaciones se concluye, por un lado, que durante este proceso se reproducen las distintas asimetrías de poder entre actores, y, por otro, que el argumento de fomentar la participación solo se utiliza cuando los conflictos han escalado.

criterion_notes.c1: No. Although background water shortages in Atenas (60% daily rationing cited from a 2014 newspaper report) motivated the state water utility's inter-cantonal water-transfer infrastructure project, the study itself examines socio-environmental conflict, community mobilization, and state-community negotiation over capturing natural spring sources in Parque Recreativo Municipal Los Chorros (Tacares), rather than household or community water or sanitation service access.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording vs. narrow 2026-10-13 reading: Under the plain wording of Criterion 2, yes—the paper examines institutional and governance processes, specifically top-down infrastructure project implementation by the national water utility (AyA) and institutionalized conflict-resolution mechanisms (direct negotiation via a technical commission and facilitation by the Defensoría de los Habitantes). Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism clarification, no—it examines conflict negotiation and citizen participation around bulk water-infrastructure siting/delivery rather than a rule-type mechanism directly governing household or community service access (eligibility screening, administrative burden, documentation or tenure requirements, tariff/cost-recovery rules, discretion/accommodation, enforcement, or utility ownership/regulatory structure governing service access). Brief mentions of an environmental amparo halting construction and park land-tenure issues relate to environmental permitting and park conservation, not household service-access rules.
criterion_notes.c3: Yes. Qualitative empirical case study drawing on primary semi-structured interviews conducted in 2019 with Tacares community actors and AyA institutional officials (including AyA's executive president), supplemented by documentary review of institutional minutes and local and national media reports.
criterion_notes.c4: No. The reported outcomes are political-conflict and negotiation dynamics—community demand articulation, adoption of technical discourse by residents, breakdown of consensus in community assemblies and facilitated talks, reproduction of power asymmetries, creation of AyA's social management unit, and completion of the infrastructure project in 2019 as initially planned—without measuring or reporting any household or community water access, connection, availability, continuity, quantity, affordability, or exclusion outcomes.
criterion_notes.c5: No. While the qualitative case-study design and conflict actors (Tacares residents/negotiators and AyA officials; conflict-process unit of analysis) are identifiable, the study lacks an eligible rule-type service-access exposure and lacks an empirical water/sanitation service-access outcome.
criterion_notes.c6: Yes. Full text is in Spanish with an English abstract; direct translation/comprehension from the provided Spanish full text is feasible per Criterion 10 (assessed directly from the Spanish full text by the AI screener), so language does not prevent full methodological and substantive assessment.

study_design: Qualitative case study (semi-structured interviews and documentary review of institutional minutes and media reports)
population_and_sample: Community actors in Tacares (Grecia canton, Alajuela province) and institutional officials of the Instituto Costarricense de Acueductos y Alcantarillados (AyA), Costa Rica (qualitative case study citing 4 key-informant interviews conducted in 2019 plus institutional minutes and media reports; unit of analysis: socio-environmental conflict and negotiation process)
exposure: Top-down implementation of an inter-cantonal water-capture infrastructure project (Mejoras al Sistema de Abastecimiento de Atenas) by AyA and subsequent conflict-negotiation processes (direct negotiation with Comisión Técnica Negociadora and facilitation by Defensoría de los Habitantes)
outcome: Socio-environmental conflict and negotiation outcomes: failure to ratify a negotiated consensus, completion of the infrastructure project in 2019 as originally designed, community adoption of technical framing, and reproduction of power asymmetries between state and community actors
rationale: Excluded as E01 (Wrong topic), with concurrent failure on C2 (narrow rule-type exposure) and C4 (service-access outcome). Although water rationing in Atenas is noted as background context for why Costa Rica's water utility (AyA) initiated a bulk water-transfer infrastructure project in 2012, this political-science qualitative case study investigates socio-environmental conflict, social mobilization, and state-community negotiation processes over tapping natural springs in Parque Recreativo Municipal Los Chorros (Tacares), rather than household or community water service access (c1=no). Under the 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 clarification, it examines top-down project delivery and conflict-negotiation/facilitation processes rather than a rule-type legal or administrative mechanism governing household or community service access (c2=no). Finally, its empirical findings concern negotiation dynamics, technical framing, and power asymmetries rather than water access, connection, reliability, quantity, or affordability outcomes (c4=no).
